controlName: Risks and Benefits for All Components
purpose: Ensures risk assessment covers every component of the AI system, including third-party software and data — not just the parts the organization built itself.
summary: Risks and benefits are mapped for all components of the AI system including third-party software and data, ensuring that risk assessment doesn't stop at the boundary of internally-developed code and instead accounts for the full composition of the deployed system.
expectedStatementElements: How risks are identified for third-party models, libraries, and data sources that are part of the system
How the benefits and risks of each component are weighed, not just the system as a whole
How the organization maintains visibility into what components make up the deployed AI system
Whether risk assessment was performed at the component level or only at the whole-system level
evidenceExamples: Component-level risk assessment covering third-party models, data, and libraries
Bill of materials or component inventory for the AI system
Documentation showing benefits and risks were weighed per component, not just overall
Risk assessment history showing when component-level review occurred
commonGaps: Risk assessment only covers the system as a whole, ignoring individual third-party components
No component inventory exists, so it's unclear what's actually inside the deployed system
Third-party components are assumed low-risk without individual assessment
Component-level risk isn't revisited when a dependency is updated or replaced
interviewQuestions: Was risk assessed for each third-party component individually, or only for the system as a whole?
Do you have a full inventory of what components — models, data, libraries — make up this system?
How do you know a given third-party component is actually low-risk, versus just assuming it?
What happens to your risk assessment when a component gets updated or swapped out?
